prs.title: feat: tickets and comments surface
prs.reference_body:
## Summary

Adds the tickets HTTP surface — the core of the product — on top of the domain-management foundation. One `tickets` feature module, organization-scoped and reachable by every authenticated role, following the established `Controller → Service → Prisma` shape.

- **`tickets/`** — `POST /tickets` (created against a same-organization customer; defaults to `OPEN`/`NORMAL`), `GET /tickets` (paged, filterable) and `GET /tickets/:id`, `PATCH /tickets/:id` (subject/description/priority), `PATCH /tickets/:id/assignment`, and `PATCH /tickets/:id/status`.
- **comments** — `GET /tickets/:id/comments` (paged, oldest-first) and `POST /tickets/:id/comments`, handled as a nested resource of a ticket (`TicketCommentsService`) inside the same module.

## Ticket lifecycle (ADR 0011)

Status changes go through a dedicated endpoint governed by a single legal-transition map in the service — the one authority on which moves are allowed:

- `OPEN → PENDING, RESOLVED` · `PENDING → OPEN, RESOLVED` · `RESOLVED → OPEN (reopen), CLOSED` · `CLOSED → OPEN (reopen)`
- An illegal move returns **409** and names the offending transition.
- `closedAt` is maintained only by this logic: set when a ticket enters `CLOSED`, cleared when it leaves — so it always reflects the most recent close and is `null` whenever a ticket is active. Editing a ticket's subject/description/priority is a separate route, keeping the transition rules in one place.

## Authorization, assignment & comments (ADR 0012)

Working tickets is every agent's job, so the coarse guard is `JwtAuthGuard` alone (no `@Roles` restriction) for reading, creating, updating, assigning, transitioning, and commenting. The real protection is organization scoping, enforced in the service beside each query:

- Every ticket, customer, assignee, and team is looked up scoped by the caller's organization; anything in another organization is invisible and returns **404, never 403**.
- **Assignment** is nullable and validated: `assigneeId` must be a same-organization user and `teamId` a same-organization team; either may be sent as `null` to unassign, or omitted to leave unchanged (a missing target → 404).
- **Tickets are not deletable** — `CLOSED` is the terminal record state; support tickets are kept as history rather than purged.
- **Comments** are always written by the authenticated agent. `authorType` records whether a comment is the agent speaking (`AGENT`, default, attributed to the caller) or the agent recording something on the customer's behalf (`CUSTOMER`, attributed to the ticket's customer) — e.g. logging a call or a forwarded email; there is no customer sign-in. `isInternal` marks an agent-only note. Comments are append-only in this iteration.

## Conventions reused and extended

- **List envelope** — reuses the shared `{ data, page, pageSize, total }` / `paginate()` convention. The ticket list is the first to extend `PageQueryDto` with resource-specific filters: `?status=&priority=&assigneeId=&teamId=` alongside the existing `?q=` (free text over subject).
- **Errors** — no new error types: `NotFoundError`→404, `ConflictError`→409 (illegal transitions), and the global `ValidationPipe`→400 for bad/unknown fields and invalid enum values. Responses are built from explicit interface DTOs (`mapTicket`, `mapComment`); no Prisma row is returned raw.
- **No migration** — the `tickets` and `ticket_comments` tables already exist in the schema; this phase is application code only.

## Testing

Two tiers, mirroring the existing suite:

- **Service unit tests** against a real Postgres — organization isolation across two seeded organizations, customer/assignee/team validation on create and assign, unassign-via-null, every legal status edge plus representative illegal edges (→409), `closedAt` set on close and cleared on reopen, comment authorship (agent default vs on-behalf-of-customer), the internal flag, and paged comment listing.
- **`supertest` integration tests** — a happy path (create → assign → resolve → close), `401` unauthenticated, `404` cross-organization isolation, `409` illegal transition, a filtered-list body, agent and customer-attributed comments, and cross-organization comment isolation.

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test` are green locally (120 tests across the repo; 100 in `apps/api`) and in CI.

## Follow-ups (non-blocking)

- `PATCH /tickets/:id/status` reads the current status then writes the next — the same read-then-write shape noted on the previous PR. Concurrent transitions on one ticket could interleave; worth folding into a single guarded update later if it ever matters.
- The list `q` filter searches the subject only; broadening it to description (or customer) is a small, additive change if the need arises.
- Comment editing/deletion and any customer-facing authorship path are deliberately out of scope here and would be separate, separately recorded decisions.
- Notifying an assignee or watchers when a ticket is assigned or commented is a natural next step now that these events exist.

prs.title: feat: notifications and queue
prs.reference_body:
Adds asynchronous ticket notifications.

- `packages/queue` — BullMQ-over-Redis plumbing (typed job, connection/producer/worker factories).
- `packages/notifications` — the notification domain: a `Transport` interface + `ConsoleTransport`, a pure renderer, a `NotificationService` that records a `Notification` then enqueues, and a `deliverNotification` consumer.
- `workers/notification-worker` — consumes delivery jobs and sends via the console transport.

Ticket assignment and comments record a `Notification` and enqueue delivery; the worker sends and records SENT/FAILED. Enqueue is best-effort so a Redis outage never fails a ticket action. No schema migration. Decisions in ADRs 0013 and 0014. Domain logic is unit-tested against a real Postgres and the assignment/comment flows have integration tests; no test requires Redis.

prs.title: feat: web foundation and the agent ticket workflow
prs.reference_body:
Adds `apps/web`, a Next.js (App Router) client for agents.

## What's included
- **Auth** — login stores the JWT in an httpOnly cookie; every API call is made from the Next server (server components + route handlers), so the browser never holds the token and the API needs no CORS change. Middleware guards the app routes; expired sessions are cleared and redirected to `/login`.
- **Screens** — login, ticket list with status/priority filters, and ticket detail with the comment thread plus status, assignment, and commenting actions.
- **UI** — Tailwind CSS with a small set of local components (`Button`, `Badge`, `Field`).

## Notes
- The API is unchanged — this consumes only endpoints that already exist.
- Decisions recorded in ADRs 0015 (App Router web client), 0016 (httpOnly-cookie BFF session), and 0017 (expired-session handling).
- Failed mutations surface an inline error instead of silently reverting; a shared client helper centralizes that.

## Testing
Components and the server client are unit-tested (Testing Library + a stubbed fetch); route handlers are covered. No test needs a browser or a live API. Full workspace green: typecheck, lint, build, and 129 tests (web 35 + existing 94), prettier clean.
